items.title: 15.5 Basic organization of human nervous system

source_refs.note: Topic 15.5 (PDF 36); Figure 15.8 is replaced by the original diagram.

blocks.text: The human nervous system has two parts: the central nervous system (CNS), the brain and spinal cord, and the peripheral nervous system (PNS), the cranial nerves arising from the brain and the spinal nerves arising from the spinal cord.

The nerves form sensory and motor pathways. There are two motor pathways: the voluntary (somatic) nervous system, which controls skeletal muscles, and the autonomic nervous system, which controls involuntary muscles and glands; the autonomic system has sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions.

blocks.alt: A tree diagram. The nervous system divides into the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord) and the peripheral nervous system (12 pairs of cranial and 31 pairs of spinal nerves). The PNS divides into sensory and motor pathways; the motor pathway into the somatic (voluntary, skeletal muscles) and autonomic (involuntary, smooth muscles and glands) systems; the autonomic into sympathetic (fight or flight) and parasympathetic (rest and restore).
blocks.caption: Basic organisation of the nervous system (original diagram after Figure 15.8).
blocks.long_description: The CNS is the brain and spinal cord. The PNS is the cranial nerves from the brain and the spinal nerves from the spinal cord. Its sensory pathways carry impulses from receptors to the CNS and its motor pathways from the CNS to effectors. The somatic system controls skeletal muscles and is voluntary; the autonomic system controls smooth muscles and glands without our will, through its sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions.

blocks.prompt: Which division would control your heartbeat, and which your choice to raise a hand?
blocks.explanation: Heartbeat: the autonomic nervous system (involuntary). Raising a hand: the somatic (voluntary) nervous system acting on skeletal muscles.

items: CNS: brain and spinal cord. PNS: cranial and spinal nerves, in sensory and motor pathways; motor = somatic (voluntary) + autonomic (sympathetic, parasympathetic).
